flagged.issue: The fact omits the page's requirement that you be employed by the federal government.
flagged.suggested_fix: You are exempt when you are employed by and driving a federal-government-owned non-commercial vehicle and possess a valid federal-agency license.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the class 3 age and graduated-program requirement but does not state the provisional age-16 and permit-period requirement.
flagged.suggested_fix: On this page, a class 3 license requires age 17 and, if under 18, completion of the graduated licensing program.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the 6-month provisional requirement but does not state the 180-day permit requirement.
flagged.suggested_fix: On this page, a driver under 18 must hold the provisional license at least 6 months before class 3 eligibility.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the limited-purpose limits but does not state that a REAL ID license works as federal identification.
flagged.suggested_fix: On this page, the limited-purpose license is not acceptable for official federal purposes and does not establish eligibility for employment, voter registration or public benefits.

flagged.issue: The page requires two residence proofs but does not say legal name, birth date, presence and SSN each need one separate document.
flagged.suggested_fix: Applicants must provide documents proving legal name, date of birth, legal presence, SSN, and two proofs of Hawaii principal residence.

flagged.issue: The cited page states class 1 for mopeds and class 2 for motorcycles with tests but does not describe class 3.
flagged.suggested_fix: On this page, class 1 is for mopeds and class 2 for motorcycles, each requiring a special knowledge test and off-street skills test.

flagged.issue: The page states the six-month hold but omits the numeric minimum age.
flagged.suggested_fix: You must hold a provisional license for six months before applying for a driver's license; the page states no numeric minimum age.

flagged.issue: The page supports the weight and passenger limits but does not mention autocycles in the class 3 description.
flagged.suggested_fix: Class 3 covers any single vehicle with a GVWR of 18,000 pounds or less and vehicles designed to transport 15 or fewer passengers including the driver.

flagged.issue: The statement omits the page's exceptions for ambulances and new vehicles.
flagged.suggested_fix: All motor vehicles must have a PMVI at least once a year, except ambulances every six months and new vehicles not until two years after initial inspection on first sale.

flagged.issue: The page states the hand-signal rule for directional signals but does not state any rule about brake lamps or head lamps having no hand-signal substitute.
flagged.suggested_fix: If the directional signals fail, use hand signals until you can have them repaired.

flagged.issue: Page 21 states the 30-day notice but does not state the in-writing and old/new address, license, make and VIN details on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: On the cited page, whenever the address is changed the owner must within 30 days notify the appropriate county agency; for full notice contents see the continuation on the next page.

flagged.issue: Page 23 supports the temporary-permit limit but does not state the Hawaii annual twelfth-month expiry on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: On the cited page, a permit allows operation up to its expiration date but never beyond twelve months; the annual twelfth-month expiry is stated on the first-registration page, not this page.

flagged.issue: Page 22 supports the new-vehicle rule but does not state the used-vehicle title, registration and notarized bill rule on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: On the cited page, Hawaii accepts for a new vehicle from another jurisdiction either the manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale; cite the later page for used-vehicle requirements.

flagged.issue: Page states driver is the only element that can gather information and act, but does not state environment and vehicle are conditions the driver must manage.
flagged.suggested_fix: The driver is the only one of the three elements who can gather information, apply skill, knowledge, experience and judgment, and take action.

flagged.issue: The page says slower traffic should, not must, use the extreme right lane.
flagged.suggested_fix: When moving slower than other traffic you should drive in the extreme right lane.

flagged.issue: The page requires two or more lanes in each direction, not just in your direction.
flagged.suggested_fix: You may pass on the right on a paved street or highway with two or more lanes marked for traffic in each direction.

flagged.issue: The page says you should not drive between procession vehicles, not must not.
flagged.suggested_fix: You should not drive your vehicle between the vehicles in a funeral procession.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the 100-foot rule but does not state the 700 to 1000 feet hill/curve rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Passing is banned within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel; the 700 to 1000 feet hill/curve rule is on a different page.

flagged.issue: The page does not state that left-turn yield applies regardless of who arrived first.
flagged.suggested_fix: At simultaneous arrival yield to the car on the right, while a left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic close enough to be a hazard.

flagged.issue: The cited page does not state the right-shoulder ban; it is on another page.
flagged.suggested_fix: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or on the listed multilane roads; do not pass on the right shoulder per the no-passing rules.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the emblem rule but does not state the no-passing pennant rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: The slow-moving emblem rule is as stated; the yellow no passing zone pennant on the left side is stated on another page.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the double solid white rule but does not state the single solid white rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Split the claim: cite page 34 for the single solid white rule and page 35 for the double solid white rule.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the yellow-line rule but does not state the white-line rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 33 for yellow lines separating opposite directions and page 34 for white lines separating same direction.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the two-way left turn lane rule but does not state the double solid yellow rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 36 for the two-way left turn lane and page 33 for double solid yellow lines allowing crossing only for a left turn.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the railroad crossing markings but does not state the red marking rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 38 for railroad crossing markings and page 35 for red markings indicating a roadway that must not be entered.

flagged.issue: Omits the page's condition that traffic is moving to the left and the stop requirement for the left turn, and adds any street.
flagged.suggested_fix: After stopping, right on red is allowed unless prohibited, and left on red is allowed from a one-way into a one-way where traffic is moving to the left unless prohibited.

flagged.issue: Page 41 states the Red X rule but does not state the red arrow rule on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: A Red X means you must not use that lane because it is used by opposite-direction traffic; cite page 40 for the red arrow meaning.

flagged.issue: Page 40 states the green-light yield rule but does not state the right-on-red yield rule on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; cite page 39 for yielding to all pedestrians and vehicles on right turn on red.

flagged.issue: The page qualifies yellow as almost always diamond, which the statement omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: Yellow warns of hazardous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond, while orange warns of road work on rectangular or diamond signs.

flagged.issue: The cited page states pass with care ends the zone but does not state do not pass begins one.
flagged.suggested_fix: A pass with care sign indicates the end of a no-passing zone, while a do not pass sign indicates locations on two- or three-lane roads where passing is prohibited.

flagged.issue: The cited page supports the exclusion-sign part but does not state the other-regulatory-sign wording on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to restrict or prohibit vehicles, movements or other activity.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the location/service function but does not state the green, blue, brown or yellow colors.
flagged.suggested_fix: Guide and information signs contain information regarding your location and the location of places and services.

flagged.issue: Page 54 states the $5,000 medical-bill lawsuit threshold but does not state the $3,000 crash-reporting threshold.
flagged.suggested_fix: For bodily injury you can sue or be sued only when medical bills exceed $5,000, among other conditions stated on the page.

flagged.issue: Page 53 states suspension for safety-responsibility non-compliance but does not state forfeiture of registration for insurance-law violations.
flagged.suggested_fix: The penalty for non-compliance with the safety responsibility law is suspension of the driver's license.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the .02 zero-tolerance rule but does not state the .08 administrative-revocation rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: The under-the-influence threshold is .08 percent or more, while the zero-tolerance threshold for drivers under 21 is .02 or more.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the 30-day permit for .08 or refusal but does not state the one-, two- or four-year refusal revocation periods.
flagged.suggested_fix: A test showing .08 or more or refusing the test results in license taken away with a 30-day temporary driving permit.

flagged.issue: The cited page 58 does not state driving with one arm out the window; that phrase is on page 57.
flagged.suggested_fix: The inattentive driver talks to a passenger while gesturing, pays little attention to traffic, daydreams or gazes off the road when alone, and forfeits safety.

flagged.issue: The cited page does not mention a mother or before birth; it only shows Use lap-shoulder belt Low and snug.
flagged.suggested_fix: Use the lap-shoulder belt low and snug, and after birth the baby rides in a car safety seat and is never carried in arms.

flagged.issue: The cited page lists Infant facing forward as a mistake and Infant position but does not state rearward.
flagged.suggested_fix: A baby rides in an infant seat or convertible seat in the infant position, while facing an infant forward is a listed common mistake.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the two-second count but does not state the rear-tires stopping gap.
flagged.suggested_fix: State only the two-second minimum following interval on this page; cite page 70 for the rear-tires stopping gap.

flagged.issue: The cited page supports the hazard-flasher claim but does not state the every-turn-and-lane-change rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Hazard flashers warn of a vehicle in a hazardous position and must never be used while moving.

flagged.issue: The cited page supports the 18-inch start and 2-foot clearance but does not state the 12-inch curb rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Parallel parking starts 18 inches from the front car and ends with bumpers at least two feet from neighbors.

flagged.issue: The cited page states greater steering effort but does not state never give up on steering.
flagged.suggested_fix: Partial loss of steering control with power steering may occur, requiring greater effort on the steering wheel to control direction.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the opposite-direction procedure but does not state the missed-exit rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Needing the opposite direction means going to the next exit, leaving and re-entering; the missed-exit continue-to-next-exit rule is on the next page.

flagged.issue: The page assigns the right-edge glance to bright oncoming lights, not to dawn and dusk generally.
flagged.suggested_fix: During dawn/dusk turn low beams on so others see you; if an approaching vehicle's lights are too bright, flash once and look at the right edge.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the turning-in-front cause but does not state that intersections are where it most often happens.
flagged.suggested_fix: Limit the claim to page 89: over two-thirds of car/motorcycle crashes result from a car driver turning in front of the motorcyclist.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the 3-foot passing rule but does not state the 3-foot parked-car rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: A driver passing a bicyclist keeps at least three feet of clearance until safely past.

flagged.issue: The cited page states waiting for the next cycle but does not state the prohibition on entering when vehicles are close by.
flagged.suggested_fix: A pedestrian should wait for the next cycle when the green has been showing for a while.

flagged.issue: The cited page states walking on the left facing traffic but does not state riding on the right with traffic.
flagged.suggested_fix: A pedestrian walks on the left side facing oncoming traffic.
